basis: Hyperphalangy, toe malformations and severe pectus excavatum define a skeletal malformation syndrome.
EBV-associated neoplasia; tumour sites vary across lymphoproliferative, epithelial and mesenchymal subtypes, without a shared organ of origin.
Carcinoma arising in the caecal epithelium.
Localized cutaneous histiocytic infiltration; normolipidemic and usually without systemic disease. Oral lesions are rare.
Developmental disability and fifth-digit/nail defects define CSS; cleft palate 2/3. Visual impairment 1/2 and hearing loss 1/3 omitted by cap.
Acromesomelic skeletal dysplasia affecting limb bones; no additional organ involvement established.
Umbrella disorder of the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes; no shared infectious or immune mechanism.
SERAC1 spectrum includes metabolic encephalopathy; sensorineural deafness occurs in roughly 80% of classic MEGDEL cases, though milder forms vary.
Unilateral congenital duplication of the thumb is a skeletal malformation.
Immune-mediated chronic arthritis. Uveitis affects fewer than 30% across the JIA umbrella; systemic manifestations are subtype-dependent.
Direct irritant injury to skin; inflammation does not establish an autoimmune or immune-mediated mechanism.
Carcinoma originating in intrahepatic bile ducts; signet-ring morphology does not change its organ of origin.
Endometriotic lesions confined to the fallopian tube affect a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Metaphyseal and vertebral osteosclerosis define disease. Developmental delay in one case does not establish common neurologic damage; ID/seizures are occasional.
Disorder of cerebrospinal fluid pressure. Occasional hearing loss or abducens palsy does not establish common additional organ damage.
Brain, renal and optic nerve malformations are defining; alopecia occurs in 80-99%. Skeletal, hearing and gut defects (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Deafness, cataract and retinal degeneration define the syndrome; sperm abnormalities are reproductive and outside the axes.
Vestibular Meniere disease affects the inner-ear vestibular apparatus.
Infection directly occupies and damages the intervertebral disc space.
Purely psychiatric chronic mood disorder without defining damage to an organ axis.
Developmental disability and skeletal abnormalities define phenotype; visual impairment 3/4. Definition and HPO disagree on limb morphology; cardiac defects each 1/4.
Neurodevelopmental and brain abnormalities with defining visual disease: optic atrophy 4/7 and rod-cone dystrophy 3/7. Other organ findings are below 30%.
Bilateral hypofunction of the inner-ear labyrinth.
Demyelinating peripheral neuropathy causes lasting distal muscle atrophy in 20/20 patients and frequent foot deformities; respiratory involvement is not established as common.
Malignant mixed epithelial and fibrous tumour originating in the uterine corpus, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
